# Actual mixed depth can be below half the sum of own maximal depths

This is an exact counterexample to the proposed stronger inequality

    max_(y in S) inf_(closed H containing y) mu(H)
                         >= 2^(-n) sum_z A(K_z),       (1)

where A(K) is the ordinary UNNORMALIZED maximal halfspace depth
of the uniform convex body K. It has n=1, d=8, three full positive
fibers, and rational polytope data. A finite thirteen-cap cover
controls ACTUAL cap volume, not a constrained own-depth capacity.

The source itself satisfies OC, with room to spare. Thus the
counterexample rejects (1), not the OC target using Gamma_d times
total volume. All quantities below are unnormalized unless a
division by V is explicitly shown.

## 1. A centrally symmetric polytope with exact rational volume

Put

    d=8,  N=9,  b=1/9,  Gamma=(8/9)^8,
    B={x in R^8:x_i>=0, sum_i x_i<=1},  V=|B|=1/8!.

Write S=x_2+...+x_8, and define the full-dimensional polytope

    D={x: 0<=x_i<=1/9 for i=2,...,8,
          0<=x_1<=11/18,
          7/18<=x_1+S<=1}.                            (2)

It is contained in B. It is centrally symmetric about

    c_D=(11/36,1/18,...,1/18).                         (3)

Indeed reflection in (3) interchanges each pair of coordinate
bounds in (2), and sends the sum of all coordinates to 25/18
minus that sum, interchanging its bounds 7/18 and one. The center
strictly satisfies every defining inequality, so D is full-dimensional.

For a fixed (x_2,...,x_8), its x_1-section has length

    11/18 - |S-7/18|.                                (4)

This stays positive on the entire seven-dimensional base cube:
its minimum at S=0 or S=7/9 is 2/9. If U_1,...,U_7 are independent
uniform variables on [0,1] and T=sum_i U_i, then

    |D|=9^(-7) [11/18-(1/9) E|T-7/2|]
       =900611/7934371614720.                         (5)

For completeness, the expectation in this calculation is exact:

    E|T-7/2|
      = (2/8!) sum_(k=0)^3 (-1)^k binom(7,k)(7/2-k)^8
      =113149/184320.                                (6)

To derive (6), symmetry gives E|T-a|=2 E(a-T)_+ at a=7/2.
On the positive orthant, integrating (a-sum u_i)_+ gives a^8/8!:
it is the volume of the positive eight-dimensional simplex
sum u_i+v<=a after adding one integration coordinate v. Excluding
u_i>1 by inclusion-exclusion gives the sum in (6); terms k>=4
vanish. This proves (5) without numerical integration.

The useful exact comparison is

    2^7 |D|/(Gamma V)=6304277/4194304 >3/2.            (7)

## 2. Three actual convex-compatible fibers with known own depths

Set

    lambda=49/50,
    q=Gamma V/[2^7 lambda^8 |D|]
      =163840000000000000000/209509599832532483477,
    C=2 lambda diag(q,1,...,1) D.                      (8)

Both q and lambda lie strictly between zero and one. For q this
also follows without large-integer evaluation: Bernoulli gives
lambda^8 >=1-8/50=21/25, so (7) yields
2^7 lambda^8 |D|/(Gamma V)>63/50>1.

The body C is centrally symmetric, with

    |C|=2 Gamma V,
    c_C=(11 lambda q/18,lambda/9,...,lambda/9).        (9)

Every coordinate is nonnegative, sum_i x_i<=2 lambda, and

    max_C x_i=2 lambda/9 for i=2,...,8.                (10)

Now take the centrally symmetric small cube

    epsilon=1/1000,   A=[0,epsilon]^8,
    a=|A|=epsilon^8,  alpha=a/V=40320/10^24.           (11)

The actual ambient body is

    mathcal C=conv( {-1} times A,
                    {0} times B,
                    {1} times C ) subset R x R^8.    (12)

Its integer fibers are exactly A,B,C. In fact (A+C)/2 lies in B:
all coordinates are nonnegative and their sum is at most

    8 epsilon/2 + lambda =123/125<1.                  (13)

In an arbitrary convex combination at integer base zero, the
endpoint coefficients are equal. Their contribution is a scaled
copy of (A+C)/2, so (13) ensures that the middle section adds
nothing to B. The extreme sections are exactly A and C, and the
base projection is [-1,1]. All three fibers have positive eight-
volume, so (12) is a full nine-dimensional convex body. It is
also exactly the hull of its mixed-integer source.

For any full centrally symmetric body, its center has ordinary
depth half its volume, and opposite through-point caps show that
no point has larger depth. The standard simplex has ordinary
maximal depth Gamma times its volume. Consequently

    A(A)=a/2,       A(B)=Gamma V,       A(C)=Gamma V.   (14)

The right side of the proposed inequality (1) is therefore

    tau=(A(A)+A(B)+A(C))/2=Gamma V+a/4.                (15)

## 3. Nine low-budget ACTUAL caps cover the whole middle simplex

Use barycentric coordinates lambda_0(x)=1-sum_i x_i and
lambda_i(x)=x_i for i=1,...,8. To avoid confusing these functions
with the scale lambda=49/50, retain their subscripts throughout.
Define

    k=7/(81 Gamma),   ell=2/(81 Gamma),
    b_h=1/9+k alpha,  b_l=1/9-ell alpha.               (16)

They lie in (0,1), and

    2 b_h+7 b_l=1.                                   (17)

For the two coordinates i=0,1 use the closed ambient caps

    H_i={lambda_i(x)-2z>=b_h}.                        (18)

They contain ALL of A and NONE of C. At A the added term is
two: x_1>=0 and lambda_0>=1-8 epsilon suffice. At C the subtracted
term is two: lambda_0<=1 and x_1<=2 lambda<2 suffice. Thus their
actual masses are exactly

    mu(H_i)=V(1-b_h)^8+a,       i=0,1.                (19)

For the remaining seven coordinates put

    beta=epsilon/2-lambda/9,
    H_i={x_i+beta z>=b_l},       i=2,...,8.            (20)

The maximum scalar value on EITHER endpoint is
epsilon/2+lambda/9. It is strictly less than b_l. Indeed
Gamma>1/3 gives ell<1/3, and alpha<1/1000, whence

    b_l-lambda/9-epsilon/2
      =1/450-1/2000-ell alpha
      >1/450-1/2000-1/3000=1/720>0.                  (21)

These caps therefore exclude both endpoint fibers, including
their boundaries, and have actual mass

    mu(H_i)=V(1-b_l)^8,       i=2,...,8.               (22)

Their traces cover ALL of B. If a middle point were outside all
nine closed caps, every barycentric coordinate would be strictly
below its corresponding threshold. Their sum would be less than
2b_h+7b_l=1, contradicting that the coordinates sum to one.

All nine masses are strictly less than tau. Here is a simple
rational bound instead of a numerical small-parameter argument.
Let c=8/9. The exact derivative identity is 8c^7=9 Gamma.
Both k and ell are less than 1/3, alpha<1/1000, and the arguments
c-k alpha and c+ell alpha lie in (0,1). The second derivative
of x^8 on [0,1] is at most 56. Taylor's inequality therefore gives

    (c-k alpha)^8+alpha
          <=Gamma+(2/9)alpha+(28/9)alpha^2,
    (c+ell alpha)^8
          <=Gamma+(2/9)alpha+(28/9)alpha^2.            (23)

The linear coefficients use 9 Gamma k=7/9 and
9 Gamma ell=2/9. Since alpha<1/1000,

    1/4-2/9-(28/9)alpha >37/1500>0.                   (24)

Combining (19), (22), and (23)--(24) bounds every middle-cover
cap mass by less than tau-(37/1500)a.

## 4. Four more caps cover every endpoint candidate

For A use its two x_1 half-caps, isolated by finite base tilt:

    J_A^+={x_1-epsilon/2-2(z+1)>=0},
    J_A^-={-x_1+epsilon/2-2(z+1)>=0}.                  (25)

At z=-1 these cover A and each has mass a/2. At B, where
0<=x_1<=1, both are strictly empty; at C, where 0<=x_1<2,
both are also strictly empty. Thus their ACTUAL source mass is
exactly a/2.

Write c_1=11 lambda q/18, the first coordinate of c_C. It lies
strictly between zero and one. For C use

    J_C^+={x_1-c_1+2(z-1)>=0},
    J_C^-={-x_1+c_1+2(z-1)>=0}.                        (26)

They cover C and each has mass |C|/2=Gamma V, by its exact
central symmetry. The same coordinate bounds show that they
strictly exclude A and B. Their actual source masses are thus
exactly Gamma V.

Both a/2 and Gamma V are strictly below tau. Together (18),
(20), (25), and (26) are THIRTEEN fixed closed ambient caps
covering the entire mixed source. This proves

    max_(y in S) inf_(H contains y) mu(H)
      <= Gamma V+(2/9)a+(28/(9V))a^2
       < Gamma V+a/4=(1/2) sum_z A(K_z).              (27)

The endpoint masses are below the first upper bound as well:
a/(2V)=alpha/2<Gamma and Gamma V is its baseline. The gap in
(27) is at least (37/1500)a. Closed boundary candidates are
included by the explicit cap cover; no minimizing-cap attainment
or numerical maximization is used.

## 5. Relation to OC and to the earlier capacity obstruction

The total source mass is

    M=(1+2 Gamma)V+a.

At the actual centroid of the exposed C fiber, every containing
ambient cap has mass at least A(C)=Gamma V. This already exceeds
the OC target Gamma M/2, because alpha<1/1000 and Gamma<2/5
give alpha<1-2 Gamma. Hence this is explicitly NOT an OC
counterexample.

Unlike `candidate 325d279c18e3a49e`, no cap
volume in this proof is replaced by a constrained own-depth
supremum. The middle traces in (19) and (22) are their exact
simplex cap volumes, all endpoint incidences are verified, and
the endpoint covers in (25)--(26) have their exact volumes.
The new conclusion is failure of the stronger ACTUAL-MASS
inequality (1).
